title: Add PRD requirements for prompt-set drift detection and regression rollback criteria
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Background: During the 2026-02-18 production incident a model rollout combined with an unseen prompt distribution shift and an unnoticed kernel quantization micro-regression produced elevated hallucination rates and customer-facing quality regressions. The postmortem (link in attachments) recommended two class-level product requirements: (1) formalize a prompt-set drift detection requirement (PRD) so we can detect semantic prompt distribution changes that correlate with quality regressions, and (2) codify automated rollback and release-gating criteria tied to prompt-set quality regressions and regression-run thresholds. This ticket updates the PRD to encode those requirements, acceptance criteria, and a phased rollout plan.
proposed_prd_changes: Add "Prompt-Set Drift Monitor" as a required evaluation signal per model profile: continuous hourly measurement of prompt embeddings centroid shifts, token distribution KL, and success-rate delta on targeted prompt-sets.
Define a two-tier regression detection: Quality Alert (soft) and Regression Gate (hard) with specific thresholds and minimum sample windows.
Require model rollouts to include mandatory preflight regression runs against canonical prompt-sets and automated post-deploy synthetic checks for the first 60 minutes of traffic.

Specify automated rollback triggers: Regression Gate exceeded on primary prompt-set OR >2 independent failure signals (prompt-set drift + LLM perplexity increase + increased rejection rates) within 30 minutes.
Ship an operator-visible dashboard card in Console that surfaces prompt-set drift metrics and regression gate status for each deployment.
Define customer communication playbook: auto-notify affected tenants when Regression Gate triggers and provide temporary fallback to verified compatible model variant.
acceptance_criteria: Prompt-Set Drift Monitor implemented and deployed for at least two model profiles (e.g., chat-medium, embed-large) and collecting data for 7 days.
Regression Gate algorithm validated in staging: triggers on injected drift scenarios and on recorded historical incident traffic replay.
Automated rollback action executes in staging and production can be validated end-to-end by PRs: rollback enactment, rollback telemetry, and customer notification flow.
Console dashboard card shows drift delta, trigger history, and current gate state for active routes.
Runbook updated with clear operator steps, SLAs for response, and a follow-up post-deploy checklist for rollouts that hit a soft Quality Alert.
out_of_scope: Full integration of user-provided custom prompt-sets for entirely managed tenants (handled in a follow-on ticket).
Building a new training pipeline to fine-tune models in response to detected drift (future roadmap).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Design and instrument prototypes for drift metrics on staging traffic; implement dashboard mockups.
Phase 2 (3 weeks): Implement Regression Gate logic and automated rollback hooks; run chaos-injection tests in canary.
Phase 3 (2 weeks): Pilot on 10% traffic for two non-critical model profiles; iterate thresholds.
Phase 4 (1 week): Full rollout to production with runbook training and on-call drills.
risks: False positives from drift detectors could trigger unnecessary rollbacks and customer-impacting flapping.
Insufficient sample sizes for low-traffic tenants may make per-tenant gates noisy; mitigation requires tenant-aggregation rules.
Runtime cost of continuous embedding comparisons at high QPS could increase serving costs unless we use sampling/approximate methods.
open_questions: What canonical prompt-sets should be maintained per model profile and who owns them (Docs vs. Model Onboarding team)?
What SLO budget do we allocate for a single-trigger rollback vs. composite-trigger rollback?
Should prompt-set drift be exposed as a public metric via the Usage API or remain internal?
